reviews.title: Such a flexible and useful learning tool!
reviews.text:
This app has so many options that make it so useful. The option to add a picture and audio is awesome!   The learning curve is not too bad. And the spaced repetition is amazing.  Yes, it takes some time to develop your own cards, but there are lots of decks already made.  I cannot recommend this app enough for study. It really helps the learning to stick.  

Just a tip, because it took me some time to figure out:  sometimes I want to practice my deck front to back, and sometimes I want to practice my deck back to front. There may be a different way, but the easiest way I have found is to go into the deck settings and drag the back side content onto the front and the front side content onto the back.  This reverses the entire deck very quickly.

reviews.title: Hoping It Improves
reviews.text: On my first few sessions I noticed they were pronouncing the Hiragana“ha” character incorrectly when it is used as a topic-marking particle.  It should be pronounced as “wa”.  I am a beginner learner with Japanese, and this is a basic understanding in Japanese sentence structure and composition, so I was a little surprised with the error and how often it is used incorrectly.  I have issued several suggestions to correct it , and I hope they do because I really enjoy the simplicity of the flashcard learning style app.  Also I was very surprised that this hasn’t been corrected sooner as the app was recommended by several Japanese Learner YouTubers.  When it is fixed I will change my rating to a “5”Star. Best regards.

reviews.title: Needs one feature for 5 *
reviews.text: This is generally a good and reliable app and has lots of flashcards sets for download. However, one feature it doesn't have unless you're creating your own flash card set is the ability to alternate which side of the card shows first. Most of the cards show from the language you're trying to learn to the language you currently use, and I would like the option to alternate. It's a lot easier to look at the new language and interpret the native language meaning, but it's a lot harder to start with the native language and remember the new one.

reviews.text:
I’m really enjoying this app and how simple yet useful it is. It’s pretty much exactly what I was looking for in a spaced repetition flashcard app and it’s free! 

My only suggestion is creating a widget for this app that also shows a streak of how many days you’ve consistently logged in. I’m trying to build a habit of reviewing my flashcards daily and a feature like that where I see the streak on my home screen would make the habit-building so much easier.
